standard.title: Iterate and communicate designs
standard.description: Generate, iterate and communicate design ideas, decisions and processes using technical terms and graphical representation techniques, including using digital tools
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can generate and communicate design ideas and decisions using appropriate attributions, technical terms and graphical representation techniques (AC9TDE4P02). They have generated and communicated ideas. They have not yet iterated — systematically refining designs based on evaluation — or used the full range of representation techniques including scale, symbols, digital mapping and modelling tools.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students generate a range of design ideas, iterate and improve them based on evaluation, and communicate decisions and processes using technical terms and graphical representation including digital tools.

nodes.label: Generating design ideas using prior knowledge and research
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can generate a range of design ideas for a product, service or environment drawing on prior knowledge, skills and research
nodes.minimum_width: Generate at least two distinct design ideas for the same need, drawing on prior knowledge and at least one research source
nodes.typical_width: Generate a range of design ideas for products, services or environments using prior knowledge, skills and research; represent ideas through sketches, diagrams or models; consider functional, aesthetic and sustainability dimensions across ideas
wider: Generate design ideas for an eco-friendly alternative to a non-recyclable product used in a community event — researching what sustainable alternatives exist before generating original ideas
Generate design ideas for an animal enclosure using modelling applications — iterating the layout and features based on the animal's environmental and behavioural needs

Consider the social values and ethics of clients when designing an environment — interviewing users of a space or seeking permission for designs/images from others, including respect for cultural and intellectual property

response_modes.reason: Students who only ever design the first thing they think of have a narrow ideation repertoire. Accumulated experience generating ideas across different product, service and environment types — each with different constraints — builds the range students can draw on when a novel design problem is encountered.

success_criteria: Generates at least two meaningfully distinct design ideas
Ideas are grounded in at least one source of prior knowledge or research

nodes.label: Representing design ideas using technical terms and graphical techniques
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can represent and communicate design ideas using appropriate graphical techniques — including scale, symbols, plans, aerial views and digital tools
nodes.minimum_width: Represent at least one design idea using a labelled diagram or plan that includes at least one graphical convention (scale, symbols, or codes)
nodes.typical_width: Represent design ideas using a range of techniques — plans with scale and symbols, pictorial maps, aerial views, digital mapping tools or infographics; use appropriate technical terms when describing designs to others; select the representation technique that best communicates the design intent
wider: Use a digital modelling or mapping application to represent a design idea — for example, designing the layout and features of an animal enclosure or a community garden using digital tools
Create an infographic that presents research and design ideas to others — combining visual representation with supporting data and technical terms
Represent a design using pictorial maps and aerial views, explaining why this technique communicates the spatial relationships better than a flat plan

response_modes.reason: Students default to a single familiar representation technique (e.g. a labelled sketch) regardless of what the design problem needs. Different design contexts that call for different techniques — aerial view for a garden layout, diagram with symbols for a circuit, 3D model for a structure — build representation repertoire.

success_criteria: Uses at least one graphical convention (scale, symbols, codes, or aerial view) in a design representation
Uses technical terms to describe at least one design decision
nodes.hinge_reason: A design idea that has not been clearly represented using graphical conventions cannot be systematically analysed or modified in N3 — iteration requires a stable, readable design artifact to work from. Students who cannot represent ideas cannot iterate on them.

nodes.label: Iterating designs based on evaluation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse and modify a design idea to improve it — iterating based on sustainability, function or feedback
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one weakness or gap in a design idea and describe a modification that addresses it
nodes.typical_width: Analyse a design idea against functional, sustainability and aesthetic criteria; modify and develop the design to improve it — documenting what changed and why; use materials, tools or equipment experimentally to refine design decisions before committing to a final approach
wider: Analyse eco-friendly alternatives to non-recyclable decorations for a community event — iterating the design to improve sustainability while maintaining function and aesthetics
Use modelling (physical or digital) to test and iterate a design idea — for example, trialling material joining techniques or component arrangements before making final choices
Replace a paper-based process with a digital equivalent (e.g. newsletters with online formats) — iterating the design to meet the same communication need more sustainably

response_modes.reason: Iteration integrates the evaluation from node 1 (what are the criteria?) and the representation skills from node 2 (how to document changes?) into a design improvement act. Students who generate and evaluate but don't modify have completed analysis but not design iteration — the modification is the learning.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The physical and digital modelling contexts are rich — they give iteration a visible, testable form where the modification's effect on performance can be observed, which makes the iterate-to-improve cycle concrete rather than abstract.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one design weakness based on a criterion
Describes a modification that addresses the identified weakness and explains why
